title: Prompt Builder, templates, inputs, outputs, and evaluation
objectives: Explain Prompt Builder as the Setup workshop where you create, test, preview, and activate reusable prompt templates.
Choose Sales Email, Field Generation, or Flex from Help's template types using the intended inputs and outputs.
Describe merge-field, flow, Apex, and object inputs, and why preview/evaluation happens before Activate.
Refuse invented edition or SKU gates; mark them Needs verification unless Help cites them.
diagnostic_question: Sales wants a personalized follow-up email, Service wants a Case summary written into a field, and a BA wants one generation that reads Opportunity plus a PDF. Before reading, which Prompt Builder template type, inputs, and evaluation step would you pick for each?
definition: Prompt Builder is where you create, test, review, customize, and manage prompt templates that connect CRM data to an LLM. Templates are reusable, use-case-driven prompts. Inputs can include merge fields, flows, Apex, related lists, objects, files, and free text depending on type. Outputs are the LLM response used in email, a record field, an invocable action, or an agent step. Evaluation means previewing a real record before you Activate. ([Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm); [Create a Field Generation Prompt Template](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_field_gen_prompt_template.htm); [Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))
why_it_matters: A Field Generation template will not send email. A Sales Email template will not write Case.Subject. Activating without preview is how hallucinated summaries reach production. Interviewers listen for template type, inputs, outputs, and a named evaluation step—not 'we turned on Einstein.'
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a print shop that runs wedding invitations. Prompt Builder is the shop. The template is the invitation form. Inputs are the guest list, venue card, and optional RSVP note you drop into the slots. The output is the printed card—an email draft, a field value, or a Flex packet. Evaluation is reading a proof against one real couple before you print the whole run. Activate is sending the job to the press, not the proof.
deeper_explanation: Help describes Prompt Builder as the place to create, test, review, customize, and manage prompt templates that incorporate CRM data from merge fields that reference record fields, flows, related lists, and Apex, connecting the user and data securely to LLMs. Assign the Prompt Template Manager permission set to admins who create and manage templates. ([Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm))

Cited template types: a Sales Email prompt template lets the sales team draft personalized emails for a contact or lead. A Field Generation prompt template brings generative workflows to fields on Lightning record pages so users can populate a field with an LLM summary or description. A Flex prompt template accepts a variable number of inputs of different object types—for example a newsletter from product and campaign objects. ([Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm); [Create a Field Generation Prompt Template](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_field_gen_prompt_template.htm))

Field Generation setup in Help: Setup → Prompt Builder → New Prompt Template → Field Generation, name the template, select the object field Einstein should populate, write the prompt, then Preview Settings with a sample record. Help notes Dynamic Forms are required to add the template to a Lightning record page. ([Create a Field Generation Prompt Template](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_field_gen_prompt_template.htm))

ASA Help: AI agents and other generative features use prompt templates from Prompt Builder. Merge fields add changing data such as names and prices; you can also add flows and Apex. You can call a prompt template via an invocable action on the platform or using Connect REST API or Connect in Apex. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm); [Prompt Builder](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_about.htm))

Evaluation in this lesson means the Prompt Template Workspace preview: pick a record, generate a response, inspect the resolved prompt, then Activate only after the proof is acceptable. Do not invent numeric quality scores Help did not cite. Grounding with retrievers is AI-004. Exact add-on SKUs remain Needs verification.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Prompt Builder authors reusable prompt templates. Sales Email drafts contact or lead mail. Field Generation writes a Lightning field. Flex takes mixed inputs. You preview a record, then Activate. Agents can call the same templates.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the output. If a human sends mail to a Contact or Lead, that is Sales Email. If a field on the record page should fill, that is Field Generation and it needs Dynamic Forms. If I need Opportunity plus a file or free text, that is Flex. Inputs are merge fields, flows, Apex, objects—not a chat channel. Evaluation is the workspace preview against a LAB_ record, not a vibe check. I never confuse Prompt Builder with Agentforce Builder.

terminology.plain: The Setup workshop for reusable LLM prompt forms.
terminology.precise: Help: create, test, review, customize, and manage prompt templates that incorporate CRM data and connect securely to LLMs.
terminology.example: Setup → Prompt Builder → New Prompt Template for LAB_ Case summary.
terminology.non_example: Agentforce Builder, which configures the agent catalog.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Process Builder: retired automation, not Prompt Builder.

terminology.plain: A reusable, use-case-driven prompt with slots for CRM data.
terminology.precise: Metadata you author in Prompt Builder; agents and other generative features consume it.
terminology.non_example: A one-off question typed into a public chatbot.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Subagent instructions: agent job guardrails, not a template type.
terminology.boundary: The template is metadata; the generated paragraph is not stored until a field or email uses it.

terminology.plain: A template that drafts a personalized email for a contact or lead.
terminology.precise: Help: lets the sales team create drafts of personalized emails for a contact or lead.
terminology.example: Draft follow-up for LAB_ Contact after a demo.
terminology.non_example: Writing Case.Description on the record page.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flex used to build a multi-object newsletter rather than a Contact/Lead email.
terminology.boundary: The human still reviews and sends unless a later feature automates send—do not invent send rules.

terminology.plain: A template that fills a field on a Lightning record page.
terminology.precise: Help: populate a field with a summary or description created by an LLM; Dynamic Forms place it on the page.
terminology.example: LAB_Case_Summary__c filled from Case Subject, Description, and comments.
terminology.non_example: A formula field that concatenates two text fields with no LLM.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Record-triggered Flow writing the same field deterministically.
terminology.boundary: Not all objects support Dynamic Forms.

terminology.plain: A template that takes a variable mix of object, file, or text inputs.
terminology.precise: Help: accepts a variable number of inputs of different object types, such as a newsletter from product and campaign.
terminology.example: LAB_Opportunity plus a PDF of pricing as Flex inputs.
terminology.non_example: A Sales Email template locked to Contact or Lead.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Field Generation: one target field on one object.
terminology.boundary: Related Help notes additional Flex input constraints; treat uncited caps as Needs verification.

terminology.plain: The data slots the template is allowed to read.
terminology.precise: Merge fields, flows, related lists, Apex, objects, files, or free text depending on type and Help for that type.
terminology.example: Opportunity.Description merge field on a Flex template.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Outputs: what the LLM returns after generation.
terminology.boundary: Grounding retrievers as dynamic inputs are AI-004.

terminology.plain: What you do with the LLM response.
terminology.precise: An email draft, a field value, an invocable/API result, or an agent action response—not the template metadata itself.
terminology.non_example: The prompt template record in Setup.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Preview panel text that was never saved to a field.

terminology.plain: Proving the template against a sample record before Activate.

interview_questions.question: What is Prompt Builder, and how do templates, inputs, outputs, and evaluation fit?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Prompt Builder is the template workshop. Templates are reusable prompts. Inputs are merge fields, flows, or Apex. Outputs are email, a field, or an invocable result. Evaluation is previewing a record before Activate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote Help: create, test, review, and manage templates that connect CRM data to LLMs. I pick type from the output—Sales Email, Field Generation, or Flex. I bind inputs so we are not hard-coding names. I preview a LAB_ record, read the resolved prompt, then Activate and assign Prompt Template User. Agents may call the same template; that does not make Prompt Builder the agent canvas.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Case_Summary Field Generation previewed on Case LAB-0001 before Activate.
weak_answer_warnings: Calling Process Builder the same tool

interview_questions.question: When do you choose Field Generation versus Sales Email versus Flex?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Field Generation writes a Lightning field. Sales Email drafts Contact or Lead mail. Flex takes mixed objects, files, or free text. The output destination picks the type.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse to pick Flex as a default 'powerful' type. If the UX is a field on the record page, Help's Field Generation path plus Dynamic Forms is the fit. If sellers need an email, Sales Email is the fit. If the packet needs Opportunity and Campaign, Flex is the cited type. If they actually need a conversation with jobs, I leave Prompt Builder and design an agent.
interview_questions.example: Case summary field vs Contact follow-up email vs product-plus-campaign newsletter.
follow_ups: Does Field Generation need Dynamic Forms?

interview_questions.question: How do you evaluate a prompt template before users trust it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I use the workspace preview with a sample record, generate a response, inspect the resolved prompt, and only then Activate. I do not invent a numeric score Help did not publish.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Field Generation Help is explicit: Preview Settings, choose a record, generate, review. I pick LAB_ records that include messy comments so I can see hallucination. If the model invents a warranty, I tighten instructions or add grounding later (AI-004). I also check that Activate plus permission sets is what actually exposes the control, not preview alone.
interview_questions.example: Preview Case LAB-0001; reject a summary that names a product not on the Case.
tradeoffs: More merge fields vs shorter prompts
follow_ups: What if preview looks good but users still cannot see it?
How is this different from Testing Center?
weak_answer_warnings: Activate from the prompt text alone

interview_questions.question: Users cannot see Field Generation on the Case page. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check Activated status, Prompt Template User access, Dynamic Forms on a supported object, and that the template targets the intended field.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's placement path is Dynamic Forms on LWC-enabled objects. If the object is not supported, I do not fight the page—I record Needs verification and consider Flex plus an invocable path. I do not grant Modify All Data to 'make AI appear.' I also confirm we did not build a Sales Email template and expect it on the Case highlight panel.
interview_questions.example: Template still Draft; tester lacked Prompt Template User; Case page was a standard layout without Dynamic Forms.
tradeoffs: Dynamic Forms migration vs another output path

interview_questions.question: How do Agentforce agents use Prompt Builder?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Agents consume prompt templates for generative steps. Merge fields, flows, and Apex can enrich those templates. Prompt Builder is not the channel and not the subagent list.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: ASA Help states agents and other generative features use Prompt Builder templates. A standard action such as Answer Questions with Knowledge uses a template plus retrievers (AI-004). A custom action can invoke a Flex template. I still design subagents in Agentforce Builder. Mixing the two Setup maps is a common interview fail.
interview_questions.example: Escalate subagent action calling a Flex template that summarizes the Case for the human.
tradeoffs: Shared template vs prompt pasted into instructions

interview_questions.question: Preview invents a closed-won amount. What do you change first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I inspect the resolved prompt: which merge fields actually rendered. I tell the template not to invent missing numbers, and I add only the fields that exist. I do not Activate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Hallucination is a generative risk Trust Layer helps limit but does not erase (AI-005). If Amount was never in the inputs, the model is guessing. I add the field or I instruct 'if Amount is blank, say unknown.' If they need Knowledge policy, that is grounding/retrieval, not more adjectives in the prompt. Evaluation is refusing Activate until the proof is honest.
interview_questions.example: Resolved prompt showed Subject and Description only; Amount was never merged.
follow_ups: When do you add a retriever?
weak_answer_warnings: Activate anyway because the tone sounds on-brand

interview_questions.question: Why not hard-code the account name in the template?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Because the template is reusable metadata. Help's point of merge fields is changing CRM data such as names and prices. Hard-coding one LAB_ name makes every other record wrong.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat the template like a mail-merge form. Inputs resolve at run time from the record, flow, or Apex. That is also why preview must use more than one sample record. Hard-coding is the fastest way to look clever in a demo and fail in week two. Secrets never go in the prompt text.
interview_questions.example: Merge Contact.FirstName instead of typing 'Priya' into the Sales Email body.
follow_ups: When would you use Apex as an input?
weak_answer_warnings: Pasting a real customer name into the template

interview_questions.question: A VP wants one Flex template to replace Flow, email, field fill, and the service agent. What do you refuse?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I refuse the mega-template. Flex is for mixed inputs, not for replacing deterministic automation, inboxes, record pages, and Agentforce channels at once.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I split: formula or Flow for math (AI-007), Field Generation for the page, Sales Email for the inbox, an agent if they need conversation and jobs. Flex is the right tool when the generation truly needs multiple resources. I mark SKUs Needs verification. A single Flex will not route WhatsApp or enforce an approval.
interview_questions.example: Rejected 'one Flex to run the business'; accepted Flex for Opportunity plus Campaign newsletter copy only.
follow_ups: When is Flex the right default?
When do you escalate to an agent?
weak_answer_warnings: Agreeing to one template for every surface
